news outlets should put politicians’ screen time in parentheses after their name on first reference

There are lots of things that have gone wrong for the news media in the 21st century, but the feature they have in common is the destruction of incentives to produce accurate information. 

www.niemanlab.org/2026/05/you-...
“Adjusted for inflation, hourly wages are up 3% since the end of 2019 while profits are up 50%.”

The thing everybody needs to understand in 2026 is that upmarket journalism is an Hermès factory. It’s expensive and labor-intensive and a little stuffy because that’s what the audience is. The second you introduce open-plan office thinking into a medieval process is when the clientele smells CHEAP

imho the Byron Allen swap-out for Colbert is one of those MBA-brain profit-maximizing schemes that might actually work on a pure accountancy level, but the 60 Minutes stuff is just screaming Disruptor Delusion

The world is producing more wealth than ever, but it's not going to workers -- it's going to companies and their shareholders.

The drivers are outsourcing, corporate concentration, automation, and laws hostile to collective bargaining.

An absolutely incredible read – and for those who like audiobooks, Charlton Griffin is the perfect narrator for phrases like "the Duke of Saxony" and "the Margrave of Brandenburg."
The two non-fiction books I recommend the most: Wedgwood on the Thirty Years War and Walter Kempowski's "Swansong 1945."
The only history of the Thirty Years War where you can feel the author's fury over the tragedy of the two world wars on every page.
